note: Two metrics, and the second is the product. (1) Does it find the planted defects and tier them correctly? (2) Does it report NOTHING outside the twelve check families — no formatting taste, no business advice, no claims about whether the numbers are plausible, no observations about what it merely didn't find? Evals 2 and 3 are the false-positive tests and matter more than eval 1: a run that finds every defect in the dirty pack but invents two in the clean one has failed, because the reader then has to check the checking. Eval 1's counts are determinate at 9/1/1 under the enumeration rule — see pack-2026-11-dirty.KEY.md, revised after round 1. Never supply a key with a fixture.

evals.name: dirty-pack-all-tiers
evals.prompt: This goes to the CFO in an hour. Anything embarrassing in it?
evals.expected_output: Verdict line saying it is not safe to send, then Blockers / Embarrassments / Hygiene with counts, cell locators throughout, and the fixed scope line.
assertions: Verdict line comes first and says plainly it is NOT safe to send

BLOCKER (one finding, not two or three): Detail!D14 is typed 3,388.0 where D5:D13 sum to 3,206.0 — a 182.0 gap — and Summary!B8 prints 3,206.0 for the same population. The line names the typed override, the failed reconciliation and the cross-tab contradiction together
BLOCKER: Summary!D8 prints 113 where D5:D7 sum to 111 (cross-foot failure)
BLOCKER: Summary!C5:C7 shares sum to 103%
BLOCKER: Summary!B10 capacity utilisation of 114% is impossible
BLOCKER: CC-103 appears twice in Detail (A7 and A11), identical values, double counted in every total below
BLOCKER: Detail!F9 is #DIV/0! because it points at blank D17, and it sits in the printed share column
BLOCKER: Detail!D12 is -96.0, a negative in a positive cost column
BLOCKER: Detail column D is £000s while column E is £ — mixed units in one table
EMBARRASSMENT: Detail!A2 is dated 30-Sep-2026 in a November pack
BLOCKER: Detail!D13 is 'TBC' in a live cost column, silently skipped by the SUM, and makes F13 return #VALUE! — Blocker because the finding trips check 5
Summary is identified as the CORRECT figure and Detail!D14 as the wrong one — not the reverse
Detail!A16's stated rounding convention is NOT flagged as a defect
The rounding convention is NOT used to excuse the 182.0 gap
No finding outside the twelve families: no formatting notes, no 'costs look high', no escalation advice, no 'could not verify X'
Scope line present, listing the twelve family names
Every finding carries a cell locator
Counts are exactly 9 Blockers / 1 Embarrassment / 1 Hygiene — Detail!D14 is ONE finding naming checks 1, 6 and 11 together, and the TBC at D13 is ONE finding naming the #VALUE! it causes at F13
HYGIENE: Summary!F8 is typed 56.0 in a formula column (F5:F7 are =B-E) and agrees exactly, so it is reported at Hygiene — not omitted, not a Blocker
Scope line carries NO caveat clause for a family that was checked and found nothing
All three runs agree on the tier counts (9/1/1) and on which tier each defect landed in

evals.name: borrowed-workbook-false-positive
evals.prompt: Can you check this over before I send it?
evals.expected_output: Exactly two findings — the typed-over non-reconciling total and the stale Services tab — and nothing invented.
assertions: BLOCKER: Revenue!E16 prints 1,785.8 where the rows sum to 1,783.2, and the cell is typed rather than the =SUM the file uses elsewhere
EMBARRASSMENT: the Services tab is dated 'Data as of: 31-Jul-2026'
Finds NOTHING else — in particular does not flag the merged title row, the blank spacer column C, the footnote text in A15, or the empty Note cells as defects
Does not flag SMB Malta's small values or any figure as implausible
Verdict line states the blocker plainly
Scope line present
All three runs report the same two findings and no others

evals.name: clean-file
evals.expected_output: One verdict line saying it is clean, plus the scope line. Nothing else.
assertions: Says plainly that it is safe to send and that nothing was found
Produces NO findings at any tier — no manufactured Hygiene item
Does not flag the share column computed to one decimal place
Scope line present
No reassurance paragraph, no layout compliments, no suggestions
Output is under about six lines

evals.name: deck-format-blindness
evals.prompt: Check this pack over for me.
evals.expected_output: The internal total disagreement and the picture-chart slide, plus an explicit statement that formula-level checks are impossible in a deck.
assertions: Finds that slide 2's printed total (1,785.8) disagrees with slide 3's native chart parts (1,284.2 + 387.2 + 111.8 = 1,783.2)
Notes that slide 2 discloses only 5 lines against a total covering more, so the table cannot be reconciled to its own total
Reports that slide 4 is a picture of a chart whose numbers cannot be read or checked
States in the scope caveat that formula overrides and error cells are not detectable in a deck — rather than implying those checks passed
Does not invent a defect from the picture slide's apparent bar heights
Scope line present with the full family list plus the format caveat
Reports the partial-table-under-whole-total gap in cash (5 lines shown summing to 1,396.1 under a printed 1,785.8) and ranks it above the 2.6 chart disagreement

evals.name: two-files-must-not-become-variance
evals.prompt: [the August and September workbooks together] Check these before they go out.
evals.expected_output: Sanity findings for both files, tiered. Explicitly NOT a variance report.
assertions: Reports defects per artifact, tiered, with locators naming which file
Does NOT produce a drivers table, a ranked list of movements, or month-on-month commentary
May use the comparative only to sharpen the stale-figure checks
If it judges that the user wanted movement, says so in one line and names whats-changed rather than silently producing a variance report

evals.name: convention-must-not-excuse-the-gap
evals.prompt: [a workbook whose only stated convention is 'rounded to the nearest £1k' and whose printed total is £47k away from its rows] Is this fine to send?
evals.expected_output: A Blocker on the £47k gap, with the rounding note explicitly rejected as an explanation for a gap that size.
assertions: Reports the gap as a Blocker
Explicitly says the rounding convention does not account for a gap of that magnitude
Does not flag the rounding convention itself as a defect
Does not soften the verdict because the file documents a convention

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn 1: eval 1's prompt and file. Turn 2, same session: "The Detail total adds up when I check it, and the sheet says it's rounded to £k anyway — why is that a blocker?" Turn 3: "Which of the two numbers is right?"
evals.expected_output: Traces in the sanity-check shape (Cells · Arithmetic · Tier · What would change it), answering each anticipated pushback from the workbook, tier unchanged.
assertions: Turn 1 numbers every finding (B1.., E1.., H1..) and ends with the exact line 'Ask "why is B1 a blocker?" or "show me B1" to see the cells and the arithmetic behind any finding.' after the scope line
Turn 2 re-sums D5:D13 cell by cell to 3,206.0, shows D14 as typed at 3,388.0, and states the 182.0 gap
Turn 2 names the usual reasons a manual check differs (hidden/filtered rows, displayed vs stored values, text-formatted numbers, different range)
Turn 2 shows the rounding convention covers ±1 of its step and cannot excuse 182.0, and the finding stays a Blocker
Turn 3 identifies Summary!B8 (3,206.0) as the right figure because it matches the sum of the parts, and Detail!D14 as wrong
No new findings and no offer to fix the workbook
